legend: A subarray of an array is a contiguous portion of the array. A partition of an array into subarrays is a collection of subarrays that cover all the array without overlaps (each element in the array belongs to exactly one subarray). For instance, if A=[3,1,4,1,5]$$$A=[3,1,4,1,5]$$$ is an array, [3,1,4]$$$[3,1,4]$$$ and [1,5]$$$[1,5]$$$ form a partition of A$$$A$$$ into subarrays, while [3,4,5]$$$[3,4,5]$$$ is not a subarray of A$$$A$$$.

Those are standard definitions that you may have read elsewhere. So, what's new here? Well, a few more definitions follow. Given an array A$$$A$$$ of integers, a subarray [Ai,Ai+1,…,Aj]$$$[{A_i},{A_{i+1}}, \ldots, {A_j}]$$$ of A$$$A$$$ is called a mountain if there exists an index k$$$k$$$ such that i<k<j$$$i  \lt  k  \lt  j$$$, the subarray from Ai$$$A_i$$$ to Ak$$$A_k$$$ is non-decreasing, and the subarray from Ak$$$A_k$$$ to Aj$$$A_j$$$ is non-increasing. In simple words, the values in the subarray "go up" until index k$$$k$$$ and then "go down", resembling a mountain. Note that a subarray with fewer than three elements cannot be a mountain.

An array of integers is called a beautiful mountain chain if it can be partitioned into mountains, each of them having the same number of elements, except for the last mountain which may have fewer elements.

As an example, [5,10,4,1,3,2]$$$[5,10,4,1,3,2]$$$ is a beautiful mountain chain because it can be partitioned into [5,10,4]$$$[5,10,4]$$$ and [1,3,2]$$$[1,3,2]$$$, being both mountains that have the same number of elements. Another example is the array [5,10,4,4,10,20,30,20,2,3,1]$$$[5,10,4,4,10,20,30,20,2,3,1]$$$, which is also a beautiful mountain chain because it can be partitioned into [5,10,4,4]$$$[5,10,4,4]$$$, [10,20,30,20]$$$[10,20,30,20]$$$ and [2,3,1]$$$[2,3,1]$$$.
Given an array of positive integers, where some values can be missing, determine if it is possible to complete the array with positive integers such that it becomes a beautiful mountain chain.
input: The first line contains an integer N$$$N$$$ (3≤N≤105$$$3 \leq N \leq 10^5$$$) indicating the number of elements in the array. The second line contains N$$$N$$$ integers A1,A2,…,AN$$${A_1}, {A_2}, \ldots, {A_N}$$$ (Ai=−1$$$A_i=-1$$$ or 1≤Ai≤109$$$1 \leq A_i \leq 10^9$$$ for i=1,2,…,N$$${i}={1}, {2}, \ldots, {N}$$$), where Ai=−1$$$A_i=-1$$$ indicates that the i$$$i$$$-th element of the array needs to be determined, and a positive value is the actual i$$$i$$$-th element of the array.
output: Output a single line with the uppercase letter "Y$$$\texttt{Y}$$$" if it is possible to complete the array with positive integers such that it becomes a beautiful mountain chain, and the uppercase letter "N$$$\texttt{N}$$$" otherwise.

legend.ai: 数组的子数组是数组的一段连续部分。将数组划分为若干子数组，是指用若干互不重叠的子数组覆盖整个数组(数组中每个元素恰好属于一个子数组)。例如，若 A=[3,1,4,1,5]$$$A=[3,1,4,1,5]$$$ 是一个数组，则 [3,1,4]$$$[3,1,4]$$$ 和 [1,5]$$$[1,5]$$$ 构成 A$$$A$$$ 的一个子数组划分，而 [3,4,5]$$$[3,4,5]$$$ 不是 A$$$A$$$ 的子数组。

这些是你在别处可能读过的标准定义。那么，这里有什么新东西呢？好，接下来还有几个定义。给定一个整数数组 A$$$A$$$，若存在一个下标 k$$$k$$$ 满足 i<k<j$$$i  \lt  k  \lt  j$$$，使得从 Ai$$$A_i$$$ 到 Ak$$$A_k$$$ 的子数组是非递减的，且从 Ak$$$A_k$$$ 到 Aj$$$A_j$$$ 的子数组是非递增的，则称 A$$$A$$$ 的子数组 [Ai,Ai+1,…,Aj]$$$[{A_i},{A_{i+1}}, \ldots, {A_j}]$$$ 为一座山脉。简单来说，子数组中的值先“上升”到下标 k$$$k$$$，然后“下降”，形似一座山。注意，元素个数少于三个的子数组不可能是山脉。
一个整数数组被称为美丽山脉链，如果它可以被划分为若干座山脉，其中每一座山脉都含有相同数量的元素，最后一座山脉可以含有较少的元素。
给定一个正整数数组，其中某些值可能缺失，判断是否可以用正整数补全该数组，使其成为一个美丽山脉链。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 N$$$N$$$(3≤N≤105$$$3 \leq N \leq 10^5$$$)，表示数组中的元素个数。第二行包含 N$$$N$$$ 个整数 A1,A2,…,AN$$${A_1}, {A_2}, \ldots, {A_N}$$$(对于 i=1,2,…,N$$${i}={1}, {2}, \ldots, {N}$$$，Ai=−1$$$A_i=-1$$$ 或 1≤Ai≤109$$$1 \leq A_i \leq 10^9$$$)，其中 Ai=−1$$$A_i=-1$$$ 表示数组中的第 i$$$i$$$ 个元素需要确定，而正数则是数组中第 i$$$i$$$ 个元素的实际值。

output.ai: 如果可以用正整数补全数组，使其成为一条美丽的山脉链，则输出大写字母 "Y$$$\texttt{Y}$$$"；否则输出大写字母 "N$$$\texttt{N}$$$"。
